analysis:
Both changed files are documentation only: docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (one table row, around line 113) and docs/architecture/inference.md (the gpt_oss row, line 1353). No source, config, endpoint, key-handling, attestation, or authorization code is touched, so no trust boundary (TB-002/003/007/009/011) behavior changes.

hardware-support.md now says the gpt-oss-20b measured activation floor (3.5 GiB) was measured while activations were float32 after layer 0, and has not been re-measured with bf16 activations. inference.md says a bf16 gpt_oss checkpoint now keeps bf16 activations and native K/V on every layer, citing GPTOSS+Experts.swift `swiglu`.

This is an availability and memory-admission point, not a regression visible in this PR. If the real bf16 activation footprint differs from the stale floor, load or KV admission could be mis-sized. The effects would be OOM or DoS-style availability risk (related to T-016/T-029) or over-conservative admission. The code change behind the doc update, the actual dtype behavior, and the floor value in UnifiedMemoryCap.swift are outside the supplied evidence. Integration should confirm that the underlying Swift/SDK change keeps `canLoad` and `loadIsServeable` post-load KV headroom checks authoritative. Those checks are described as a backstop in the invariants section. The SSD prefix cache (T-041) is not affected: the gpt-oss prefix-cache default-on statement is only repeated unchanged, and the new dtype claim does not alter cache encryption, scoping, or TTL.

No threat model update is needed beyond the documented caveat. No findings.
